description:
## Contract risk

Canonical mail-client `EmailGetParams` at
crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:58-63 carries:

```rust
/// Catch-all for vendor / site / private extension fields not covered
/// by the typed fields above. Preserves unknown fields across
/// deserialize/serialize round-trip per workspace extras-preservation
/// policy (see workspace AGENTS.md).
#[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]
pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
```

calendars-client `CalendarEventGetParams` at
crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/mod.rs:101-114 does NOT carry the
field.

The same pattern recurs across mail-client's input/param structs:
`EmailCopyParams` (mod.rs:67-84), `MailboxSetParams` (mod.rs:87-100),
`EmailSubmissionSetParams` (mod.rs:111-137), `EmailImportInput` (mod.rs:147),
`EmailParseParams` (mod.rs:253). All have the `extra` flatten field; the
calendars equivalent does not.

## Why this matters for a caller

A caller who wants to pass a vendor-defined `CalendarEvent/get` argument
(e.g. `acmeCorpExpandReducedParticipantsScopedToCalendar`) has no path:

- Cannot use struct-literal construction (the struct is `#[non_exhaustive]`;
  see sibling finding).
- Cannot use the `extra` field (the field does not exist).
- Cannot extend `CalendarEventGetParams` (private fields are not the issue
  — fields are public — but adding a field to the struct requires shipping
  a new version of the crate).
- Can only fork the crate.

This is the exact gap the workspace AGENTS.md extras-preservation policy
was designed to close: vendor / site / private extension fields should
round-trip through the wire-format types without the implementor having to
wait for an IETF revision or a workspace crate release.

Note the strict letter of the workspace policy (AGENTS.md, Extras-preservation
policy) applies to public Deserialize structs and result enums.
`CalendarEventGetParams` is Serialize-only, not Deserialize, which is the
formal reason calendars-client got away with it. But the canonical
mail-client `EmailGetParams` is also Serialize-only and DOES carry the
field — the canonical reading is that the extras pattern applies to ALL
public wire-traveling structs, regardless of direction. Calendars-client
diverges.

## What goes wrong if this stays

Once shipped at 0.x.y, adding a new field to a public struct (even a new
field with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = ...)]`) is technically
non-breaking — but the workspace pattern has been to add the catch-all
`extra` field once, so future fields don't need to keep being added. By
not adding it, the calendars-client crate signals to vendors and integrators
that calendars args are NOT extensible without crate-version bumps. That's
the wrong signal.

Plus this is a canonical-template divergence per AGENTS.md.

## Fix shape

Add the field to `CalendarEventGetParams`:

```rust
#[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]
pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
```

Note this fix requires the struct to be `#[derive(serde::Serialize)]`
(currently it is not — filed as a separate finding). Address both together.

## Source citations

- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/mod.rs:101-114
- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:40-64
title: CalendarEventGetParams lacks 'extra' flatten field — canonical EmailGetParams has it, blocks vendor extension args
